summary.title: Reduced residence time of droplet impact on heated surfaces
summary.authors: Song Rong, Shiquan Shen, Tianyou Wang, and Zhizhao Che
summary.executive_summary: This study investigates the dynamics of droplet impact on heated surfaces, identifying a novel 'bouncing-with-spray' mode that significantly reduces residence time compared to the traditional 'retraction-bouncing' mode. The research utilizes high-speed imaging and theoretical modeling to demonstrate that vapor bubble bursting within the liquid film creates holes, causing the film to recoil and fragment, thereby shortening the contact duration. Experiments with water, ethanol, and water-glycerol mixtures across nucleate, transition, and film boiling regimes confirm that this mechanism is independent of liquid viscosity. A scaling law derived from energy balance and critical bubble burst conditions accurately predicts the transition boundary between the two modes in the film boiling regime, showing a relationship where the degree of superheat scales inversely with impact velocity (ΔT ∼ V⁻¹). The findings suggest that thermal induction offers a reliable, fabrication-free method to minimize droplet residence time, with observed reductions of approximately 40% in dimensionless time, applicable to applications like spray cooling and anti-icing.

claims.description: The bouncing-with-spray mode significantly reduces droplet residence time compared to retraction-bouncing mode.
A scaling law predicts the transition between bouncing modes based on impact velocity and superheat.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study investigates the dynamics of droplet impact on heated surfaces, identifying a novel 'bouncing-with-spray' mode that significantly reduces residence time compared to the traditional 'retraction-bouncing' mode. The research utilizes high-speed imaging and theoretical modeling to demonstrate that vapor bubble bursting within the liquid film creates holes, causing the film to recoil and fragment, thereby shortening the contact duration. Experiments with water, ethanol, and water-glycerol mixtures across nucleate, transition, and film boiling regimes confirm that this mechanism is independent of liquid viscosity. A scaling law derived from energy balance and critical bubble burst conditions accurately predicts the transition boundary between the two modes in the film boiling regime, showing a relationship where the degree of superheat scales inversely with impact velocity (ΔT ∼ V⁻¹). The findings suggest that thermal induction offers a reliable, fabrication-free method to minimize droplet residence time, with observed reductions of approximately 40% in dimensionless time, applicable to applications like spray cooling and anti-icing.

Research Context
Droplet impact is ubiquitous in nature and industry. Heat transfer and phase change significantly affect impact. Reducing contact time is crucial for applications like anti-icing. Previous strategies required complex surface fabrication. Theoretical limits for contact time were previously established.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Can heat-induced vapor bursting reduce droplet residence time? Does the 'bouncing-with-spray' mode exist in boiling regimes? Is the residence time reduction independent of viscosity? Can a scaling law predict the transition between modes? Does the vapor bubble radius determine the mode transition?

Methodological Details
Three liquids were used: water, ethanol, and mixtures. Droplets were injected at approximately 4 µl/s. Impacts occurred on polished silicon substrates. Surface roughness was less than 0.5 nm. Temperature was controlled with ±1°C accuracy. High-speed imaging captured side and aerial views. Droplet sizes ranged from 1.6 mm to 3.4 mm. Impact speeds varied from 0.9 to 2.1 m/s. Weber numbers were varied from 10 to 180. Viscosity was altered via glycerol concentration. Liquid properties including density and surface tension were measured. Residence time was defined as visual contact to detachment.

Procedures And Architectures
Experimental setup included a heated copper plate. PID controller managed the substrate temperature. Matlab program analyzed high-speed images. Weber number quantified kinetic to surface energy ratio. Jakob number indicated sensible to latent heat ratio. Theoretical model assumed uniform vapor layer thickness. Energy conservation equated heat transfer to vaporization. Film thickness scaling followed Re−2/5D0 relationship. Pressure distribution was derived from Poiseuille flow. Lift force balanced droplet weight and buoyancy. Scaling law derived as ΔT ∼ V −1.

Key Results
Bouncing-with-spray mode reduced residence time significantly. Transition boiling RB mode took 12.0 ms. Transition boiling BWS mode took 6.5 ms. Film boiling RB mode took 12.0 ms. Film boiling BWS mode took 6.3 ms. Viscosity had no effect on BWS residence time. Dimensionless RB time was approximately 2.3. Dimensionless BWS time was approximately 1.4. Residence time reduction was about 40%. Scaling law agreed well with experimental data. Transition temperature increased with Weber number.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Vapor bubble bursting creates holes in the liquid film. Holes cause the liquid film to recoil. Reduced recoiling distance shortens residence time. Mechanism is similar to ridge-induced fragmentation. Fragmentation is induced by vapor bubbles in the fluid. Model explains transition in film boiling regime. Theory applies to transition boiling regime as well.

Contradictions And Limitations
Detailed numerical simulations are still needed. Scaling exponent n may vary with surface structure. Heat transfer area A was assumed constant. Open questions remain in the field.

Claims
The bouncing-with-spray mode significantly reduces droplet residence time compared to retraction-bouncing mode. Residence time in BWS mode is much smaller. Dimensionless time reduced from 2.3 to 1.4. Reduction magnitude is approximately 40%. Viscosity does not affect BWS residence time. Thermal induction avoids complex surface fabrication.
A scaling law predicts the transition between bouncing modes based on impact velocity and superheat. Scaling law agrees well with experimental data. Relationship is ΔT ∼ V −1. Scaling exponent n varies for different surfaces. Model explains transition in transition boiling regime.

Data And Code Availability
Custom Matlab program was used for analysis.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Viscosity variation showed no effect on BWS mode. Results consistent across different liquids.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows the experimental setup schematic. Figure 2 illustrates impact morphologies in three regimes. Figure 3 shows vapor bubble burst sequence. Figure 4 demonstrates viscosity independence. Figure 5 compares dimensionless residence times. Figure 6 presents theoretical model and regime map. Table 1 lists liquid properties.

Three Takeaways
1. Heat-induced vapor bursting creates a new bouncing mode. 2. Residence time reduction is ~40% and viscosity-independent. 3. Scaling law ΔT ∼ V⁻¹ predicts mode transitions.
